rationale: All devices went offline simultaneously at 7 AM after a router replacement, with the base station showing online=false, uplink=no_internet, and E-503 in logs. The base station LED was solid red, and moving the Ethernet cable to a LAN port plus power-cycling the router and base station restored the LED to solid blue and brought all devices back online. This confirms the base station had lost its network uplink due to the cable being in the wrong port on the new router.

repair_steps: Confirm the base station LED is solid blue and all devices show online in the app.
Verify the Ethernet cable is plugged into a LAN port (1-4) on the router, not the WAN/Internet port.
Advise the customer to keep the router and base station powered on and avoid moving the cable.
Document the resolution: router replacement caused wrong port connection; power-cycle restored uplink.
Close the case as resolved at frontline.

args.action: Ask the customer to check the Ethernet cable from the base station to the new router: it must be plugged into a LAN port (usually numbered 1-4), NOT the WAN/Internet port. If unsure, have them move the cable to a different LAN port. Then power-cycle the router (wait 2 minutes), then power-cycle the base station, and check whether the LED turns from solid red to a normal colour and devices come back online in the app.

results.text: The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.
